title: Cyber Resilience Act product security
description: Questions for the product security owner and repository checks for products with digital elements under Regulation (EU) 2024/2847. These rules do not establish conformity.

sources.title: European Commission, The Cyber Resilience Act: summary of the legislative text

rules.instruction: Ask the legal owner whether the product is a product with digital elements made available on the EU market, and whether the organization acts as manufacturer, importer, distributor or open-source software steward (Art. 3).
rules.verification: Link the recorded answer from the change.

rules.instruction: Generate for each release a software bill of materials in a commonly used machine-readable format that covers at least the top-level dependencies (Annex I, Part II, point 1).
rules.verification: Find the SBOM attached to the release and check that it lists the shipped top-level dependencies.

rules.instruction: Keep a coordinated vulnerability disclosure policy and a contact address for reporting vulnerabilities (Annex I, Part II, points 5 and 6).
rules.verification: Open the published policy and check that it gives the contact address and the handling steps.

rules.instruction: Make the default configuration of the changed component secure, with a way to reset the product to its original state (Annex I, Part I, point 2(b)).
rules.verification: Install the release with default settings in a test and review the exposed services, credentials and permissions.

rules.instruction: Distribute security updates through a secure update mechanism, automatic where applicable (Annex I, Part II, point 7).
rules.verification: Check in a test that the client verifies the authenticity of an update artifact before installing it.

rules.instruction: Ask the product owner for the support period during which vulnerabilities will be handled (Art. 13(8)), and record it in the product documentation.
rules.verification: Check that the product documentation states the support period.
